page: Microsoft Azure E96ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the 64-bit ARM architecture, utilizing 96 dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 cores operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz. The physical core architecture assigns one thread per core without simultaneous multithreading, supported by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 672.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 7.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no local ephemeral storage, relying completely on external network volumes for persistent storage operations, and features no dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance testing demonstrates strong parallel compute and memory throughput. The system achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 24092.0 and a stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 198302.01. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 464.87 GB/sec, accompanied by 205.52 GB/sec for write tasks. Workloads centered on fast memory access excel, as seen in Redis SET performance reaching 170.49 million operations per second and high PassMark database operational metrics. Single-thread benchmarks operate in the average tier, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1696.0.

The architecture delivers qualitative cost efficiency by packing high memory density onto energy-efficient ARM physical cores, avoiding thread contention found in hyperthreaded systems. The primary tradeoff centers on the lack of attached high-speed local disk and modest single-core throughput. The configuration is primarily aligned with memory-heavy operations, including Redis caching layers, in-memory databases, parallel software compilation pipelines, and batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ps_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by 96 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-N2 cores clocked at 3.4 GHz with single-threaded physical cores. The instance features 672.0 GB of RAM, equating to 7.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. It does not provision local ephemeral storage or GPU acceleration, depending entirely on remote block storage for data persistence. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute, high memory bandwidth reaching 464.87 GB/sec for uncached reads, and exceptional in-memory key-value throughput with 170.49 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution speeds are moderate, the lack of hardware multithreading contention ensures predictable parallel throughput. This configuration provides strong qualitative efficiency for large memory-bound footprints, making it suitable for distributed in-memory databases, high-capacity caching layers, continuous integration build clusters, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
